model_annotation: The image displays two side-by-side bar charts illustrating public spending as a percentage of GDP (% des BIP¹) for different levels of government in Germany from 1991 to 2023, with a vertical dashed line marking the “Bahnreform²” (railway reform) around the year 2000. The left chart shows total expenditures by the federal government (Bund, blue), states (Länder, purple), and municipalities (Gemeinden, green), stacked vertically to represent the combined public sector spending, with a black line overlaying the bars indicating the total for all regional authorities (Gebietskörperschaften insgesamt). Spending peaked near 3.3% in the early 1990s, dipped after the reform, and rose again to around 2.9% by 2023. The right chart isolates the spending of regional authorities (Gebietskörperschaften insgesamt), broken down into the same three levels, but with much lower overall values — peaking at just over 0.5% in the early 1990s and declining to near zero by 2023, with the black line again showing the total. Both charts use a vertical axis ranging from -0.5 to 3.5, with gridlines at 0.5 intervals, and a horizontal axis showing years at five-year intervals. The charts visually emphasize the relative scale of federal, state, and local spending before and after the railway reform, with the left chart showing the bulk of public expenditure and the right chart highlighting the comparatively minor role of regional authorities in overall public spending.
